title: Ex 2.6 #11 · (∼P) ∧ (P ⇒ Q) vs ∼(Q ⇒ P)
prompt: Are $(\sim P) \wedge (P \Rightarrow Q)$ and $\sim (Q \Rightarrow P)$ logically equivalent? Decide, and back up your answer with a truth table, a chain of known equivalences, or a row where the two statements differ.
answer_format: equivalent or not equivalent. Steps are optional: truth-table columns, rewrite steps, or a row like P = T, Q = F where the two statements differ.
hints: Write out both columns. With two letters there are only four rows to compare.
Look closely at the last row, where P and Q are both false.
solution: $(\sim P) \wedge (P \Rightarrow Q)$ is F F T T, and $\sim (Q \Rightarrow P)$ is F F T F.
They differ in the row $P = $ F, $Q = $ F: the first statement is true there and the second is false.
So the statements are not logically equivalent.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses logical equivalence (Section 2.6).
